sentences.text: Wpcrl/147/2024 on 16 February, 2024

Author: Rakesh Thapliyal
Bench: Rakesh Thapliyal
Sl. Office Notes,
No. Date reports,
 orders or Court'S Or Judge'S Order

S  proceedings  or directions  and  Registrar's  order with  Signatures  WPCRL No.147 of 2024  Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1.
Mr. Sanjay Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioner.
2. Mr. Saurabh Pandey, learned Brief Holder for the State.

3. By the instant writ petition, the petitioner is praying for quashing of FIR dated 14.01.2024,
bearing FIR No.0014 of 2024, whereby the petitioner has been implicated for the offence punishable under Sections 376, 504 and 506 of IPC, Police Station I.T.I, District Udham Singh Nagar.

entities.text: Police Station I.T.I, District Udham Singh Nagar
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 4. It is submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that the complainant is the wife of the younger brother of the petitioner and she is having three children, residing separately.

5. It is also submitted by learned counsel for the petitioner that earlier to this, the petitioner's mother Smt. Santosh Devi, also made a written complaint to the Sub Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur on 10.11.2023, with the allegations that the present respondent no.3 is threatening to implicate her and the family members and she is habitual of leveling frivolous allegations, but in the meantime, an application was moved by the respondent no.3 under Section 156)(3) Cr.P.C., in which a police report was called, which was submitted by the Sub-Inspector on 04.12.2023 before the Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur, wherein it is contended that in the month of July 2022, the complainant- respondent was operated in Navy Hospital, Kashipur for Tubectomy and doctor opined that she cannot be pregnant.
He submits that despite this report, the Judicial Magistrate, Kashipur passed an order for registration of the FIR.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner further submits that this is nothing but the counter-blast to the complaint made by the petitioner's mother.

Furthermore, the allegation, as alleged in the FIR,
appears to be false in view of the police report dated 04.12.2023, which was submitted before the Judicial Magistrate and despite this, the Judicial Magistrate has not applied his mind and directed to for registration of FIR.

1 7.
It is further submitted that, prima facie, no offence is made out and this is a glaring example of malicious implication of the present petitioner.
8. Mr. Saurabh Pandey, learned Brief Holder for the State accepts notice on behalf of respondent Nos.1 and 2.

9. Issue notice to respondent no.3, returnable within three weeks.
10.
Steps to be taken within a week.
11. Respondents are granted four weeks' time to file counter-affidavit.
Two weeks' time, thereafter, is also granted to learned counsel for the petitioner to file rejoinder- affidavit.
12. In the meantime, the investigation may go on in respect of FIR No.0014 of 2024, however, the petitioner shall not be arrested provided he cooperates with the Investigating Agency.

(Rakesh Thapliyal, J.) 16.02.2024 R.Bisht WPCRL/147/2024 on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22200882/
